summary: Day 1 of 5 for the 11-18 risk-off call (confidence 0.55). SPY fell about 0.31% (spy_value 573.35 to 571.60; VOO -0.29%, VTI -0.26% on the day) and closed at 730.2, only 0.06% above the 729.79 200-day line. That is down from 0.36% in the morning packet. The Nvidia print did not set off the reflex rally I named as the main way the call fails, at least on the first session. The regime filter is still on, and the shared VOO/VTI stop is NEAR at +0.06% but has not tripped. The grade needs SPY to fall more than 1% from 732.44 over five sessions, which means a close below about 725.1. At 730.2 it is down about 0.31%, so the call is on track but not yet earned. The account gained $0.46 (equity 621.35) while SPY fell, so the book's low-beta single names did their job.
update: Provisional, not graded. I keep risk-off into 11-19. The SPY 200-day line is now 0.06% away, so a close below 729.79 is a coin-flip-sized move that would turn the regime filter off and sell VOO and VTI (about 23.3% of equity together: 13.3% + 10.0%) on one close. The PM has pre-committed to letting that happen, and I agree. My tilts got a mixed one-day read from holdings, not sector ETFs: the Staples names lagged a -0.31% SPY (WMT -0.41%, KR -0.89%, SAM -0.53%), and Health Care split (IDXX +1.19%, EXEL -0.31%, INCY -1.08%). WMT reports 11-19, so tomorrow tests the Staples favor more than today did. I can't call any tilt broken on one day of single-name moves; the next packet's XLP and XLV 5-day figures will settle it. Two things would change the stance: a close back above about 1% over the line (around 737) with VIXY reversing its +15.69% 5-day gain, or HYG recovering its -0.71% 5-day loss. Either would move me to neutral. Track record caveat: always-neutral would have scored 50% against my 56.2% (9 of 16), and my last risk-off after a sharp drop (11-06) was wrong on a +2.59% bounce, so 0.55 confidence still fits. No lesson in learning.json names the Market Analyst. L8 and L9 use my note as the reference, so I will keep the bonds-not-hedging and do-not-add-to-US-core lines explicit tomorrow.
